name: Slingshot
description: A slingshot toy: pull the ball back in its elastic socket, let go, and it flies on an arc, bounces off the plate's own edges and settles back into the socket.
interactionNotes: Press the ball and pull it away from the socket: the socket stretches into a capsule that hugs both circles, the arrow inside the ball turns to the direction the throw will take, and the ball trembles once the band is nearly taut. Release and the ball leaves straight back the other way, bounces off the plate's sides and top, loses height, rolls to a stop and fades back into the socket. The further the pull, the faster the throw, and it grows faster than the pull. `power` scales that speed and `bounce` sets how lively every contact is. With the ball focused, the arrow keys aim, Space or Enter throws and Escape puts it back. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the ball does not tremble and the throw leaves no dust.

props.name: power
props.description: Scales the throw, in percent. 100 is the tuned speed; below it the ball is lobbed, above it the ball is fired.

props.name: bounce
props.description: How much speed a contact keeps, 0 to 100. 0 drops the ball dead, 100 keeps almost all of it.

props.name: plateColor
props.description: Surface of the plate the ball plays on.

props.name: socketColor
props.description: Color of the socket and of the band once it is stretched.

props.name: ballColor
props.description: Ball, and the dust the throw leaves behind.

props.name: markColor
props.description: Color of the arrow inside the ball.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.defaultValue: "توپ رو بکش و رها کن؛ با کلیدهای جهت‌دار نشونه بگیر و با کلید فاصله پرتش کن"
props.description: Accessible name of the ball, for when the default Persian label does not fit the page.

tips: `power` is read at the moment of release, so changing it while the ball sits in the socket changes the next throw; `bounce` is read every frame and can be changed mid-flight.
The plate is a fixed 360 by 260 canvas and the physics is measured in those pixels, so give it a stage at least that wide instead of shrinking it.
The ball is a real focus target: arrow keys aim, Space or Enter throws, Escape puts the ball back. Keep `ariaLabel` short and in the page's language.
Dust is drawn in `ballColor` and the band in `socketColor`, so a light ball on a dark plate stays monochrome when you flip the palette.
Nothing is drawn outside the plate: the ball bounces off its own edges, so a smaller plate needs a softer throw to be playable.
